judge: Claude (an AI model), 2026-11-20. Not human judgments. Four independent passes, one per quarter of the moods, each grading from knowledge of the film with the corpus overview as a fallback.

rubric.2: squarely fits: a film a horror fan would readily name for this mood
rubric.1: defensible: fits in part, or fits a looser reading of the mood

pool: Union of: semantic top 12, unified top 12, keyword-only top 8, five noisy unified pages, and the hand-written gold films. Built by scripts/graded_eval.py pool. Extended on the same day with the films returned once keyword vectors were mixed in (239 more pairs, judged blind to which ranker returned them). Extended again with the films returned once descriptive tags were added (146 more pairs, judged from title and TMDB keywords without sight of the tags). Extended a third time with the films the production paths return with their randomness on, ten visits per mood (693 more pairs).

title_rubric: For 'title' queries the user has seen the named film and wants others. 2: a film a horror fan would readily recommend to someone who asked this; 1: defensible; 0: no. The named film itself is 0 and its sequels, prequels and remakes are at most 1 (enforced when the grades were merged). Judged by Claude (an AI model) on 2026-11-20, three independent passes of eight queries each, blind to which ranker returned a film. Pool: semantic and unified top 12 with title handling off, with exclusion only, and with the film vector at shares 0.5, 0.7, 0.85 and 1.0, plus noisy unified pages.
